newsitem.title: CHINA: China to build passageways for lonely pandas.
newsitem.headline: China to build passageways for lonely pandas.

text.p: China plans to build new nature reserves and "green passageways" to protect panda habitats and ensure lonely groups of the endangered animal can travel in search of mates, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
Saving the habitat of the giant panda was the most effective way to preserve the species, Xinhua quoted an official of the Forestry Ministry's Giant Panda Protection Office as saying.
Over the next few years, authorities would build three new nature reserves and 17 "green passageways" linking areas set aside for the panda, the official said.
The passageways would help prevent inbreeding and genetic deterioration among pandas by allowing the notoriously frigid animals to move around, he said.

"About 1,000 giant pandas in the world are now being separated into small groups by human activities and highways, and there are only three to five giant pandas in some of the smallest groups," Xinhua quoted him as saying.

China had made some progress in reducing human threats to the areas where pandas lived and already had 25 nature reserves set aside for them, but a lack of funds was hampering efforts to ensure the species' survival, he said.
The death of large tracts of bamboo, the staple food of the giant panda, was another serious threat, he said.
From 1983 to 1996, as many as 183 pandas suffering from illness or malnutrition were found in the wild, he said.
